manuscript_title: Response geometry under community reorganization: richness-sensitive regimes and state-dependent branching
significance_statement: Ecological syndromes are often summarized as directional average responses, but that summary can conceal the mechanism that determines which branch an individual lineage realizes. In a frozen plant–pollinator model, exact control of realized richness shifts the ensemble mean response while substantial lineage-level branching persists, showing that coarse regime placement and branch identity are distinct operations. A prespecified finite-community audit then shows that the relative importance of plant starting state and realized community is itself scale dependent: realized community dominates in small stochastic systems, starting state becomes increasingly important as community sampling stabilizes, and branching disappears only in the deterministic mean-field limit. The numerical crossover is model-specific; world and Izu evidence bound biological plausibility and historical identifiability rather than calibrating it to nature.
ethics_statement: Not applicable to new data collection in this manuscript. The study reports simulations, a source-audited synthesis of published literature, and secondary analysis of published plant–pollinator data; it includes no new field sampling, specimen collection or experimental work requiring new approvals, licences or permissions.
data_availability: Primary numerical results derive from frozen synthetic simulation outputs, exact realized-richness controls, finite-community system-size audits, exact finite-k moment calculations, a prespecified relational-robustness audit, a frozen 25-entry source-readiness audit and secondary analyses of published island plant–pollinator data. The anonymous reviewer archive contains the journal-facing manuscript, Supporting Information, interaction-kernel audit, response-geometry and threshold results, realized-richness and system-size robustness materials, deterministic figure inputs, source-readiness records and analysis scripts needed to inspect the reported claim boundaries. Data and custom code supporting review are prepared for first submission in the anonymous reviewer archive; before final publication, accepted code and frozen analysis materials will be deposited in the Dryad Digital Repository with a persistent DOI.
